name: hh-meanrev-micro: post-shock vol-contraction re-entry (15m)
rationale: MECHANISM: same two-stage 'wait for vol to roll over' fade as the 5m variant — buy the washout dislocation only once vol_realized crosses DOWN from its post-shock peak (forced flow exhausted, spreads re-tightening), never mid-cascade — but on the 15m bar, where the vol-contraction signal is smoother/less noisy and the ensuing reversion is larger relative to cost. This tests whether the vol-mean-reversion timing edge is timescale-robust. Entry: bb_z extreme AND vol_realized crossing DOWN through a fitted level AND rsi below a floor. Long-only spot; exit as bb_z reverts. DISCONFIRMER: if 15m vol-contraction timing does not beat entering at the 15m spike, the refinement is dead at this timescale too. LEAKAGE: the cross-down must be from closed bars only — a 1-bar-lag re-run that kills the edge means look-ahead. If 15m and 5m give the same net result, they are duplicates — keep one.
catalyst: fade entered as 15m realized vol rolls over post-washout
